Reverse transcriptase can synthesize DNA from an RNA template without a separate primer because it has an intrinsic RNase H activity and often uses the 3' end of the RNA or a tRNA molecule as a primer.  
A DNA or RNA primer is not strictly required to be added separately in the case of retroviral reverse transcription, since the enzyme itself can initiate DNA synthesis using the RNA template.  
Thus, only reverse transcriptase is needed for synthesis of an RNA/DNA hybrid from a single-stranded RNA template.  

Final answer: (D)
